title: Honest Scales and a Generous Hand

verses.text: Dishonest scales are an abomination to the LORD, but an accurate weight is His delight.
When pride comes, disgrace follows, but with humility comes wisdom.
The integrity of the upright guides them, but the perversity of the faithless destroys them.
Riches are worthless in the day of wrath, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.
The righteousness of the blameless directs their path, but the wicked fall by their own wickedness.
The righteousness of the upright delivers them, but the faithless are trapped by their own desires.
When the wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the hope of his strength vanishes.
The righteous man is delivered from trouble; in his place the wicked man goes in.
With his mouth the ungodly man destroys his neighbor, but through knowledge the righteous are rescued.
When the righteous thrive, the city rejoices, and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.
By the blessing of the upright a city is built up, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.
Whoever shows contempt for his neighbor lacks judgment, but a man of understanding remains silent.
A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.
For lack of guidance, a nation falls, but with many counselors comes deliverance.
He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer, but the one who hates indebtedness is secure.
A gracious woman attains honor, but ruthless men gain only wealth.
A kind man benefits himself, but a cruel man brings trouble on himself.
The wicked man earns an empty wage, but he who sows righteousness reaps a true reward.
Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuit of evil brings death.
The perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but the blameless in their walk are His delight.
Be assured that the wicked will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will escape.
Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
The desire of the righteous leads only to good, but the hope of the wicked brings wrath.
One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.
A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
The people will curse the hoarder of grain, but blessing will crown the one who sells it.
He who searches out good finds favor, but evil will come to him who seeks it.
He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like foliage.
He who brings trouble on his house will inherit the wind, and the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.
If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!

context.author: Solomon, named in the heading “The proverbs of Solomon” (10:1). The collection runs from 10:1 to 22:16, about 375 sayings.
context.genre: Wisdom sayings: two-line proverbs, most of them contrasts
context.audience: Anyone learning to live wisely, first the young men of Israel’s court and households
context.mapLabel: JERUSALEM, THE ROYAL COURT OF SOLOMON
context.setting: The chapter opens in the market: “Dishonest scales are an abomination to the LORD, but an accurate weight is His delight” (v.1). It goes on to pride and humility (v.2), integrity that guides the upright (v.3), and a city that rises or falls with its citizens (vv.10-11). The gossip reveals secrets but the trustworthy keep them (v.13), and safety lies in many counselors (v.14). A cluster of sayings praises generosity: one man gives freely and grows richer, another withholds and comes to poverty (vv.24-26). “The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life” (v.30).
context.custom: Goods were weighed on balance scales against stone weights, and a dishonest merchant could carry two sets, a heavy one for buying and a light one for selling (Deuteronomy 25:13-16). Grain was the main store of wealth, and a man who hoarded grain to drive up the price in a shortage was cursed by the people (v.26). A gold ring in a pig’s snout (v.22) is a picture of beauty wasted on someone without sense.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 12 turns to discipline, work, and honest and dishonest words.
context.timelineBible: The law demanded honest weights and measures (Leviticus 19:35-36), and the prophets accused merchants of using false ones (Amos 8:5; Micah 6:11). Verse 31 is quoted in 1 Peter 4:18 in its Greek form: “If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?” (1 Peter 4:18)

translation.meaning: A pair of balance pans, used for weighing silver and goods.
Literally “stone,” since weights were stones of a set size. A full weight is “a whole stone.”
Literally “a soul of blessing”: a person who blesses others.

gospelParallels.note: Whoever sows generously will also reap generously (vv.24-25).
Quotes v.31 from the Greek: if it is hard for the righteous to be saved.
Give, and it will be given to you.

otBackground.note: Do not keep two different weights in your bag.
Use honest scales and honest weights.
Merchants who cheat with dishonest scales.

overview.summary: God hates dishonest scales and pride; the upright are guided by integrity, the generous grow rich, and the righteous bear the fruit of a tree of life.
overview.settingLine: Sayings for the marketplace and the city.

history.t: Before coins, silver was weighed out.
Sellers held back grain in a famine.

customs.t: Jewelry of gold worn in the nose.

archaeology.t: Dome-shaped stone weights marked with a sign and a number are common finds in Judah.
Trade happened in the open spaces by the city gates.

overview.discussion: “One gives freely, yet gains even more” (v.24). Where have I seen generosity make someone richer in ways that matter?
overview.book: The book of Proverbs · 31 chapters. Short sayings and longer poems that teach how to live wisely in God’s world, beginning with the fear of the LORD.
overview.author: Solomon (10:1)

historicalImage.caption: Netherlandish Proverbs, painted by Pieter Bruegel the Elder in 1559 (Gemäldegalerie, Berlin). More than a hundred Dutch sayings are acted out at once in one crowded village, a reminder that every people keeps its wisdom in short, memorable lines.
